$comment: Network presets for the arcnow.io SDKs. THE single source of truth for
both languages: the maintainers' sync copies this file into
rust/src/generated/ and typescript/src/generated/, and the maintainers' pin gate
fails when a copy has drifted. Two SDKs that each carried their own address
list would eventually disagree about one address, in one language, on one
chain, and nothing would say which was right.
WHAT IS NOT IN THIS FILE. No deployer, fee-recipient or custodian address:
those are operational identities, not integration surface, and an SDK that
published them would be inviting callers to depend on them. No per-token
addresses either - a token and its curve come from the Launched log, one
pair per launch, and there are as many as there have been launches. No
third-party platforms: those arrive on PlatformRegistry.PlatformRegistered.
NULL MEANS 'NOT DEPLOYED ON THIS CHAIN'. It is not the zero address, which
on Arc is a real account that would send money nowhere at all. Both SDKs
refuse to build a call to a null address and say which contract was missing.
ONE STACK PER NETWORK (schemaVersion 4). `contracts` is the network's arcnow.io stack. Both SDKs price
only the multi-quote curve (arcnow/bonding-curve@3.x.x) and trade only under the claim-based fee hook
(arcnow/arc-now-fee-hook@3.x.x); any other version is refused by name rather than priced or traded.
`contractVersions` names the build at each address, key for key. `contracts.v4Router` is
UniswapV4Router04, bound to `v4.poolManager`; neither is arcnow.io's code.
WHILE pins.json contracts.deployment.status IS 'pending', the addresses below are the version-2
stack that is still live, recorded because they must equal the deployment record, and both SDKs
refuse them. The multi-quote stack replaces this block when it is broadcast.
QUOTE TOKENS (`quoteTokens`). What a curve can be priced in: native USDC (address 0x000...000, the
gas currency, 18 decimals) and the ERC-20s arcnow.io's quote registry allowlists. This list is
METADATA, not the allowlist: the SDKs read symbol, name and decimals from here so that labelling an
amount costs no RPC call, and they ask the registry (QuoteRegistry.isQuoteToken) whether a quote is
actually accepted. A quote the registry lists and this file does not is read on chain once per
process. `native: true` marks the one quote paid as msg.value; every other quote is pulled with an
ERC-20 allowance, in raw units of its own decimals.

arc-testnet.name: arc-testnet
arc-testnet.$explorerComment: Left null rather than guessed. Nothing in arcnow-io/contracts or arcnow-io/deployment names an explorer for Arc testnet, and a wrong link in an error message is worse than none.
arc-testnet.$deployedAtBlockComment: The block the multi-quote stack was deployed in, as arcnow-io/contracts exports/addresses.json records it. The version-2 stack it replaced was deployed at 61,911,405.

native.$comment: Arc's gas currency IS USDC, and msg.value is 18 decimals. See nativeUsdc in both SDKs.

usdcErc20.$comment: The SAME asset through an ERC-20 interface, reporting 6 decimals. It does NOT pay for gas and no arcnow.io contract reads it. Present here only so a wallet-facing UI can convert; the scale between the two is 1e12.

$quoteTokensComment: EURC is Circle's euro stablecoin on Arc testnet: a FiatToken proxy reporting 6 decimals,
blocklistable and pausable by Circle. Its symbol and decimals are read back off the chain by
the maintainers' template gate. Whether the registry accepts it is the registry's answer, not this
file's: EURC is registered on the deployed stack with a 2 EURC launch fee, and its admin can
deactivate it at any time, so both SDKs ask the registry rather than trust this list.
allowanceSlot is the storage slot of the token's allowance mapping (FiatToken's `allowed`, 10).
Both SDKs use it ONLY to state-override the router's allowance when pricing a pool buy with eth_call.
Verified 2026-09-14 by reading an override of that slot back through allowance() on rpc.testnet.arc.io,
and re-verified on every run of the TypeScript fork suite.
$contractsComment: arcnowPlatform is arcnow.io's OWN PlatformConfig - one platform among however
many the registry admits, and the default this SDK launches under when a caller
names no other. It is not privileged; it is just the one whose address is known
before you have read a log.
escrowMigrator is null and that is the better state: it is the one custodial
contract in the system, and arcnow-io/contracts deploys it only on a chain where
no venue migrator could be built. Arc testnet has a v4 venue, so none exists.
v2Migrator and v3Migrator are null because both need a wrapped-native token that
Arc testnet does not publish and arcnow-io/contracts refuses to default.
quoteRegistry is the registry this stack was deployed with. Both SDKs prefer this address,
and otherwise ask the launchpad for it (Launchpad.quoteTokenRegistry(), immutable).

$comment: WHERE A GRADUATED TOKEN IS TRADED.
poolManager is the Uniswap v4 PoolManager arcnow.io's migrator opens pools in. It is
genuine Uniswap v4 - the v4-core commit arcnow-io/contracts pins, compiled at
optimizer_runs 200 - and every token that has graduated has its liquidity there,
permanently: the positions are burned and the migrator is immutable. A v4 pool has
no address of its own; it is a PoolId inside this manager's storage.
Arc testnet also has a second, separate PoolManager (0x9BEACCac...) with a
third-party router bound to it. arcnow.io does NOT use either. Moving to that manager
would never have made the tokens already graduated here tradeable, and would have split
liquidity across two disjoint markets. Instead arcnow.io deploys its own copy of the
same router - UniswapV4Router04 from z0r0z/v4-router, unmodified - bound to this
manager. Its address is contracts.v4Router, null until it is broadcast.
While contracts.v4Router is null, both SDKs REFUSE to quote or trade a graduated token
rather than build a call to nothing. Once it is set they ask the router which
PoolManager it serves and trade only pools in that one.
NO QUOTER IS DEPLOYED ON THIS CHAIN. Both SDKs quote by eth_call-ing the router itself
with state overrides and reading the BalanceDelta it returns, which is the trader's own
delta with the hook's 1% already applied. sdk/README.md documents the method.

venues.$comment: Which graduation targets this deployment actually offers. A token graduates into the migrator its curve snapshotted at launch; ask the curve, not this list, for a particular token.

$comment: ARC MAINNET DOES NOT EXIST YET, or at least arcnow.io is not on it. Every
address below is null ON PURPOSE and this entry is here ON PURPOSE.
A preset that is absent gets a caller a 'no such network' error they read as
'the SDK is behind' and work around by pasting addresses from somewhere. A
preset with plausible addresses in it gets them a transaction to an account
that does not exist. A preset that is present, complete in shape and null in
every address gets them an error that says exactly what is true: nothing is
deployed here, pass your own addresses if you know better.
Both SDKs therefore RESOLVE this network and REFUSE to use it, naming the
contracts that are missing. Nobody invents an address to fill it in: when
arcnow.io deploys to a mainnet, the values arrive here from the deployment
record, with the contracts commit that produced them.
arc-mainnet.name: arc-mainnet
